summary: Aggamahāpaṇḍita A. P. Buddhadatta worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College and was attested as a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya in 1923.
Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, A. S. Gadre served as Director of Archaeology for the Archaeology Department of Baroda State, attested in 1944.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar was an Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941), Superintendent of Archaeology for Travancore State (1922), and served the Kingdom of Thiruvithamkoor (~1923–1934).

A. V. Williams Jackson studied at Columbia and Halle-Wittenberg under Edward Delavan Perry and Edward Washburn Hopkins. Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, he spent his career at Columbia, serving as professor from 1895 to 1935.

Aaron P. Proffitt studied at CU Boulder, the Inter-University Center, and the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback and others. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Japanology, he became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at University at Albany, SUNY (~2015).
Working in Indology, Abaji Vishnu Kathavate succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar and is attested as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2026.

Abanindranath Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art & Craft (~1905–1915), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. A specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology, he was attested as an assistant professor at the University of Peshawar in 1988.

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Abel Bergaigne studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault. He served as répétiteur at the EPHE (~1869–1877) and as lecturer and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.
Abhimanyu Rao studied under Deepak Dabral and held a post at Shiv Nadar School in the field of Indology.

An Indologist who studied under Rāmbhadrācārya, Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra headed the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, was a visiting professor at the University of Indonesia (~1987–1989), and served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~2000–2003).

Abigail I. MacBain earned an MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and others. Specializing in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she is attested at the University of Edinburgh in 2026.

A scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Anquetil-Duperron studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Dastur Darab. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1935–1939) and worked in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).
Abraham Yohannan studied at Columbia University (~1895–1898) and held a post there from ~1894 to 1925, working in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies.
Abraham Zablocki earned a PhD at Cornell University. Working in Tibetology and religious studies, he held a post attested in 2008 at Agnes Scott College.
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under U Nārada and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1955), and he taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he was a research associate at Munich (2004–2006) and is attested at Hamburg in 2026.

Achyutananda Dash works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, attested in 1999.

Adalbert Bezzenberger studied at Göttingen and Munich under Theodor Benfey, working in linguistics and Indology. He served as Privatdozent at Göttingen (1874) and at the University of Königsberg as Professor of Sanskrit (1879), Prorektor (1890–1891), and Rektor (1919–1921).
